hook_text: Pull a carrot out of the ground. Is the bit you eat a root, a stem or a fruit?
clip_script: School garden in Mthatha. Pull up a carrot. That orange bit? It is a root! Roots hold the plant and drink water. The stem holds it up, like a tree trunk. Leaves make food from sunlight. Flowers call in the bees. Then the flower turns into a fruit. Yes, a tomato is a fruit, because it has seeds inside! And every seed can grow a new plant. Six parts, from a tiny pond plant to a giant baobab.
visual_style: Whiteboard plant drawn from the soil up, each part labelled as it appears, then a row of very different plants beside it.
mood: Hands-on and cheerful, like a morning in the vegetable garden.
pacing: Build one plant part by part from the bottom up, then a quick parade of big, small and colourful plants.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find all six parts on a plant near your home.
